cases.purpose: -u (effective UID) and -U (real UID) select different processes when real and effective UIDs differ: four processes with (real,effective) = (3001,3002), (3001,3001), (3002,3002), (3002,3001) are selected by -u, -U and their combinations, by comma lists and by an account name, exactly as procps pgrep selects them.
cases.oracle: procps-ng 4.0.4 pgrep run by the reference bash side against the same processes, whose real and effective uids are set by setpriv and read back from /proc/PID/status
cases.comparison: Byte parity of status and stdout (PIDs mapped to fixture tags).

cases.purpose: killall -u selects by real UID, not effective UID: with processes of (real,effective) = (3001,3002), (3001,3001), (3002,3002), (3002,3001), -u 3001 signals exactly the two with real UID 3001, -u 3002 the two with real UID 3002; an account name (nobody) resolves through passwd and a different account (daemon) selects nothing.
cases.oracle: Requirement text (real UID); real and effective uids of each fixture are read back from /proc/PID/status
cases.comparison: Exact stdout derived from the requirement and /proc facts.
cases.stdout:
p1: real=3001 effective=3002
p2: real=3001 effective=3001
p3: real=3002 effective=3002
p4: real=3002 effective=3001
-u 3001 rc=0
state: p1=dead p2=dead p3=alive p4=alive n=alive
-u 3002 rc=0
state: p1=alive p2=alive p3=dead p4=dead n=alive
-u daemon rc=1
state: p1=alive p2=alive p3=alive p4=alive n=alive
-u nobody rc=0
state: p1=alive p2=alive p3=alive p4=alive n=dead

cases.purpose: pkill -u/-U select by effective/real UID as procps pkill does, and signalling a process owned by another user without privilege (the pkill invocation runs as uid 3000 against processes of uid 3001) fails with a diagnostic and status 1, while signalling its own process succeeds.
cases.oracle: procps-ng 4.0.4 pkill run by the reference bash side against the same processes
cases.comparison: Byte parity of status and stdout (PIDs mapped to fixture tags) and of the shape of stderr; fixture end states are read back with kill -0.

cases.purpose: pkill -c counts only the requests that succeeded: run as uid 3000, a pattern matching two processes of uid 3001 and one own process counts 1 with status 0, a pattern matching only foreign processes counts 0 with status 1.
cases.oracle: Requirement text (count and status reflect only successful requests; procps counts matches, so it is not the oracle); ownership set by setpriv and read back from /proc
cases.comparison: Exact stdout derived from the requirement.
cases.stdout:
mixed count=1 rc=0
state: own=dead p1=alive p2=alive
foreign-only count=0 rc=1
state: p1=alive p2=alive p3=alive p4=alive n=alive
